title: Exact input-fragment reconstruction
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let its state type have a binary code, and let $C,e,c,A,d$, an input word $x$, a cursor $j$, and a time $t$ be given. If $t$ is at most $c\,(A(n+C(n+1)^e+1)^d+1)^2$ for $n=|x|$, then the input fragment at time $t$ extracted from the packed encoding of $x$ with cursor $j$ equals the serialized input clause group at time $t$ for the all-false reference input of length $n+C(n+1)^e$.
hypotheses_covered: $t$ is at most the producer horizon for $|x|$
replaced: For every source machine, state code, parameters, instance $x$, cursor $j$, and time $t$ at most the producer horizon, the stored-coordinate input fragment equals the serialized fragment of the pure input clause group at time $t$ over the reference length.
